execution: CPU only; no robot/environment calls or policy training
question: Can a correctly centered future-innovation control variate lower whole-trajectory Gaussian policy-gradient variance without bias?
generator: T50 scalar additive state; terminal reward finalstate; iid Gaussian raw proposals; linear or clip(-1,+1) dynamics; theta0 sigma1.
control: Time-specific regression of return residual onto current raw Gaussian innovation. Coefficients fitted on independent training trajectories and frozen for test. Subtract future controls only; current controls require analytic score expectation correction.
comparators: current only CV with analytic correction
negative_controls: future CV with coefficient depending on its own innovation and currentstate
screen: On each of4gamma/dynamics cells: variance trace for future-only learned CV <=.75 baseline, and both estimated gradient components within4standarderrors of analytic truth. Failure requires mechanism revision before robot tests. Report exact variance ratios and CIs; do not infer sample efficiency.
analytical_truth: Mean gradient sum(gamma**remaining)*1 for linear or P(-1<epsilon<1) for clipped; logstd gradient0. For gamma1 linear exact baselines: MC covariance trace4275, future-only600, full analyticCV0.
scope: Known control-variate mechanism, not novelty or robot efficacy. Data generation/fitting time and all toy rows counted. PPO clipping/minibatch normalization are absent; no claim about their bias.
